description_en: Bistabara Śikhara Temple, located in the northern end of the village of Bistabara, dates from approx. 13th-15th centuries. A newly laid cement path leads to the monument, which is now part of a walled complex built by the village committee. The complex includes a new single-story concrete structure that will serve as a small museum. To the north is a cluster of threeśikharatemples (JUM0450,JUM0451andJUM0452). The Temple is surrounded by three stone memorial pillars (JUM0455).The monument stands alone and faces north. It is built on a large stone platform. The entrance to the now-empty sanctum used to be preceded by a small vestibule (skt.ardhamaṇḍapa). This is indicated by the presence of a stone pillar at the site. This pillar was one of the two supports for the vestibule's roof. The doorjambs and the pediment are no longer there, and the lintel is carved with three square vignettes, each with a deity's image. A two-armed deity is sitting in the lotus position on the left, a seated Gaṇeśa is in the centre, and a standing character is on the right. The stone is too eroded to identify the two deities who surround Gaṇeśa. The Temple does not have anāmalakadisc installed.From the 13th to the 15th centuries, suchśikharatemples were built throughout the Karnali Basin (Andolfatto 2019). The rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally known asdevala) complicates dating of these monuments. Given the Temple's proximity to three nearbyśikharatemples dating from the 13th to the 15th centuries, it is possible that this monument was built around the same time. This dates to the end of the Khaśa Malla kingdom (12th-14th century) and the reign of the Kalyāl dynasty from Jumla (15th century).
identified_threats: Wall cracks, Missing stones at plinths
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
